decisions.reason: It extends the firm's core wafer-substrate and packaging capabilities into higher-value semiconductor applications that fit its R&D profile and stated move toward multifunctional packaging wafers.
Carrier wafers are very close to the established business and directly match the firm's stated strategic focus on reusable handling solutions for increasingly complex wafer processing.
The Cu-interposer glass wafer is a core-adjacent advanced packaging product with visible launch effort and strong fit to semiconductor integration trends the firm is targeting.
An off-the-shelf wafer brand leverages existing materials and production know-how, broadens access to standard demand, and supports the core business with limited strategic risk.
Glass-based circuit boards are too far from the firm's narrow, precision-wafer core and likely require different markets, commercialization effort, and capabilities than its strongest business lines.
